label: input m during original phase at position >= 3
explanation: Fires on every input of the letter m in the original (pre-<DEL>) phase at position t >= 3, and on nothing else: never on m at positions 0-2, never on any other token, never at the delimiter step. Magnitude grows with position: about 0.35-0.4 of max at t=3, about 0.7 at t=4, about 0.8-1.0 at t >= 5 (top examples are at t=5-6). Repeats of m also fire (in_first is not required). The only misses are 53 tiny activations (<0.07 of max) in the copy phase when m is fed back as the copied first token (recall_idx=1), which carry ~0% of the mass.

issues: No systematic counterexample found. On the test split the predicate has zero false positives. All 65 missed steps (0.0% of mass, each under 0.07 of max) are the same case: m fed back as the copied first token at the step right after <DEL>, in sequences where orig(0)=m. That matches the explanation's stated exception.

The profile matches the factual claims: no firing at t=0-2, at the delimiter, or on any token other than m. Firing rate is a flat ~0.033 across orig_idx 3-8. Mean magnitude per t, worked out from mass share divided by active count, is about 0.40 of the peak at t=3, about 0.81 at t=4, and about 0.95-1.0 at t=5-8. The explanation's 'about 0.7 at t=4' is a little low but qualitatively right.
Minor wording point: the label says 'position >= 3' but has no upper bound. That is fine, because original-phase positions only go up to 8 (L <= 9).
